page: Microsoft Azure A2m_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Av2 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 2 vCPUs. The processor is equipped with a 50 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

This server is provisioned with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core, alongside 20 GB of local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the hardware exhibits performance characteristics in the lower tier. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 344.35 and 670.13, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 60.64 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 6.81 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and compression tests also reflect entry-level capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 954.55 and a memory score of 671.42.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the A2m_v2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio at a lower hardware tier, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high compute performance. It is positioned for lightweight database operations, basic caching layers, or small-scale web serving. Benchmark data shows a static web serving throughput of 0.89 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 1.0 million operations per second, confirming its utility for low-traffic, memory-reliant applications rather than intensive data processing or large-scale LLM inference.
